Project-code basis: repository README.md describes this as a DoLa + ENN reliability pipeline. The exact approved capstone title was not present in the supplied materials, so the title placeholder is retained as requested.
A small language model can answer questions. This project studies how decoding and uncertainty signals can help evaluate those answers.
Compare layer-contrastive decoding and Epinet-based uncertainty for TinyLlama answer generation.
A user asks a short factual question.
Contrast final-layer scores with a selected earlier layer.
Generate a response and inspect uncertainty or candidate agreement.
Python   /   PyTorch   /   Hugging Face Transformers & Datasets   /   NumPy
Methods: TinyLlama   ·   DoLa   ·   Epistemic Neural Network (Epinet)   ·   Self-consistency
Project details are based on README.md, config.yaml, main.py, run_experiment.py, Neural Network/dola.py, and Neural Network/enn_torch.py. No benchmark result is asserted.
Fluent language generation does not by itself show whether a response is correct or reliable.
A single model response offers limited evidence about answer reliability.
The project tests complementary signals at two levels: token scores across model layers and agreement across sampled answers.
Intermediate and final predictions can differ
Entropy is not automatically correctness probability

Motivation is framed as an evaluation problem, not as a claim that the project already improves reliability. TruthfulQA describes how language models can reproduce common falsehoods: Lin, Hilton, and Evans, ACL 2022, https://aclanthology.org/2022.acl-long.229/.
The implementation connects decoding, uncertainty estimation, and answer-level comparison.
Use the local TinyLlama chat model for question answering.
Select an earlier layer using Jensen–Shannon divergence and apply DoLa.
Learn a next-token correction from C4 features while keeping the base model fixed.
Compare plurality voting with ENN-entropy-weighted voting.
Evaluate exact match and calibration metrics when run outputs are available.
Evaluation is part of the objective. Performance gains remain unverified until benchmark runs are saved.
Objectives reflect the implemented commands and methods in main.py and run_experiment.py. The last objective is intentionally evaluative and makes no claim of achieved improvement.
The project combines established ideas for a local small-model evaluation pipeline.
Produces a single continuation under greedy decoding or sampling.
Contrasts mature and premature layer distributions during decoding.
Indexes predictions by a sampled epistemic variable to expose model uncertainty.
Samples several candidates and selects a normalized plurality answer.
The repository brings these components together, but the combined pipeline has no saved benchmark output yet. Its accuracy and calibration remain open questions.
References: TinyLlama (Zhang et al., 2024)  ·  DoLa (Chuang et al., 2024)  ·  ENN (Osband et al., 2021)  ·  Self-consistency (Wang et al., 2023)

Sources: Zhang et al., “TinyLlama: An Open-Source Small Language Model,” https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02385. Chuang et al., “DoLa: Decoding by Contrasting Layers Improves Factuality in Large Language Models,” ICLR 2024, https://openreview.net/forum?id=Th6NyL07na. Osband et al., “Epistemic Neural Networks,” https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.08924. Wang et al., “Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models,” ICLR 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171. These references motivate individual methods; the deck does not claim prior work validated this exact combination.
Two paths meet at evaluation: C4 trains the Epinet; questions exercise answer generation and voting.
The ENN confidence weight is an entropy heuristic. Calibration against correctness must be measured.

C4 feature preparation and document split: Neural Network/data_prep.py. Model and DoLa decoding: Neural Network/dola.py. Epinet training and sampled entropy: Neural Network/enn_torch.py. Candidate aggregation: run_experiment.py and Neural Network/self_consistency.py. The diagram represents implemented code paths, not evidence of successful trained runs. C4 background reference: Raffel et al., JMLR 2020, https://jmlr.org/papers/v21/20-074.html.
DoLa changes token scores. The Epinet samples token distributions. Voting combines answer strings.

JSD selects the premature block
Then: mature logits − α × premature logits
Output: predictive entropy and an epistemic proxy. These describe token distributions, not answer correctness directly.

Architecture details are read from Neural Network/dola.py and Neural Network/enn_torch.py. The configured TinyLlama structure uses a mature index of 21, candidate premature indices [0,4,8,12,16,20], hidden width 2,048, Epinet width 512, epistemic index size 6, and three samples by default. The diagram labels configured dimensions, not measured parameter counts.

The current contribution is an implementable comparison pipeline; empirical conclusions require the next evaluation run.
The system combines TinyLlama, dynamic DoLa layer contrast, an Epinet trained on C4 next-token features, and answer-level voting.
The repository supports evaluation on TruthfulQA and a local question set. No benchmark result is available in the inspected workspace.
